problem: The search step is wrong. Hobbs searches only the part of the subtree below X that lies to the left of the path from the pronoun up to X; if X is an S node it then searches the branches to the right of that path, without entering any NP or S it meets. As written ('Search that subtree left-to-right, breadth-first'), the search also covers the pronoun's own NP and noun phrases that come after the pronoun, so the algorithm can return a wrong antecedent. The standard algorithm also repeats the whole search in earlier sentences, most recent first, when X is the topmost S of the sentence; that step is missing entirely.
fix: Replace the step with: 'Search the branches below X to the left of the path from the pronoun, left-to-right, breadth-first, proposing NP nodes that agree; never propose the pronoun's own NP. If X is an S node, also search the branches to the right of the path in the same way, stopping at any NP or S you meet. If no antecedent is found and X is the topmost S of the sentence, repeat the whole search in the previous sentences, most recent first.'

problem: The Retain definition is not the standard one. Retain means Cb(Un) = Cb(Un−1) and Cb(Un) is not the top-ranked Cf (Cp); the top Cf may well stay the same as in the previous utterance. Saying 'top Cf changes' makes Retain and Continue look like a partition of the Cb-stays cases, which they are not.
fix: Continue: Cb stays and Cb is the top-ranked Cf. Retain: Cb stays but is not the top-ranked Cf. Smooth-shift: Cb changes and becomes the top-ranked Cf. Rough-shift: Cb changes and is not the top-ranked Cf.

problem: CoNLL-style scoring is not whole-entity scoring. Entity-based scoring is CEAF; the CoNLL shared-task metric averages link-based and mention-based scores (MUC, B³, CEAF). A student can lose marks repeating this.
fix: Write: 'Some metrics count links, as in MUC-style scoring; some score whole entities, as in CEAF; and some average per-mention scores, as in the CoNLL shared-task metric. Entity F1 and mention F1 are not interchangeable.'

problem: The chains found in steps 2 to 4 contain 5 links (2 + 2 + 1), yet step 5 says the gold standard has 2 links. The arithmetic is right for the numbers given, but the numbers do not come from the chains the student has just built, which is confusing.
fix: State that the counts are from a separate small test set, or change the counts so they match the chains: with gold = 5 links and 2 correct out of 3 predicted, P = 0.6667, R = 0.4, F1 = 0.5.

where: Worked example 1, steps 2 to 4 and the answer
problem: Set braces are used for chains that contain the same string twice, as in {Ravi, He, Ravi}. A set cannot hold duplicates, so this notation is wrong for two distinct mentions of Ravi.
fix: Write chains as ordered lists of mentions, for example (Ravi₁, He, Ravi₃), (Meera₁, Meera₃, She), (report, it), or subscript the mentions to show they are separate mentions of the same entity.

problem: The statement of Centering Rule 1 does not say which utterance's Cf and which utterance's Cb are meant, so it can be read as applying within one utterance, where it is false.
fix: Answer: 'If some element of Cf of the previous utterance is realized as a pronoun in the current utterance, then Cb of the current utterance is also realized as a pronoun in it.'
